gen-dafont-disorder-gf-port-lligat-slab: Raw, scattered, deliberately rough: Disorder holds its letters far apart. Port Lligat Slab settles underneath as a text serif with wide porthole-like counters and curves that leave room to breathe, so paragraphs move along gently.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-quando: Disorder's joins stay hair-thin, and its tall lowercase sprawls. Quando, a text serif with sparse, wide spacing and a deep middle zone, deserves a generous size so those roomy letters can stretch out.
gen-dafont-disorder-plus-jakarta-sans: Plus Jakarta Sans reads modern and precise, its monoline strokes leaving curve endings well apart and its lowercase at a moderate height. Disorder's tall, scattered letters rough up the top.
gen-dafont-disorder-sora: Jagged and restless, Disorder sets tall lowercase far apart. Sora then runs on in precise geometric lines, with a lower x-height and widely parted curves that make a long passage feel steady.
gen-dafont-dogica-fs-amulya: Dogica spaces its tall lowercase wide apart, almost shouting each letter. And Amulya follows with generous, open curves in a lower, more modern stance.
gen-dafont-dogica-fs-plein: Dogica sets its lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals, with wide tracking and openly cut curves, making it heavy and commanding. Plein, the reliable sans-serif, does the quieter work, with a clear channel leading into every round letter.
gen-dafont-dogica-fs-spline-sans: Dogica stretches its tall lowercase with wide tracking, which gives it a heavy, commanding stance. Spline Sans is the plain sans partner, approachable and contemporary, with uniform strokes and wide gaps where curves meet stems.
gen-dafont-dogica-fs-synonym: Dogica brings heavy, commanding capitals-and-near-capitals with wide tracking, and its curves stay open at every end. Synonym, a sans-serif, runs a tube-like stroke at a moderate height.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-almendra: Dogica's lowercase rises nearly to capital height, spaced wide and cut open at every curve. Almendra, the serif, brings the bookish dignity, with a deep midsection in its lowercase that suits steady reading.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-bree-serif: Dogica pushes its near-capital lowercase out on wide tracking, heavy and commanding in every line. And Bree Serif, a text serif with outsized lowercase proportions, takes over for the literary, refined reading.
